constraints: The two readers must agree for every sqlite:/// URL form: sqlite:///data/x, sqlite:///./data/x, sqlite:////data/x and sqlite:///:memory:.
The documented URL grammar must not change. sqlite:///data/x still means /data/x and sqlite:///./data/x is still workdir-relative.
validate_database_placement must keep returning the same keys, the same values and raising ValueError with the same meaning when required=True and the path is not persistent.
Do not remove or weaken the fail-closed behaviour for a non-persistent database path; the guard is the protection against the /app/data regression.
Do not add new required settings fields and do not change any existing default, including database_url and database_persistent_root.
The EMA file must keep its latency_ema.json filename.
Prefer a single owner for the URL grammar over a second corrected copy that can drift again.
known_regression: Commit 7575d2b ('fail closed on non-persistent router database paths') added the canonical resolver and left latency_cache_path untouched -- this fixture is the residual defect of that repair. The same one-off `sqlite:///` interpretation is duplicated in six other modules in that repository, so a repair which 'fixes' this by inlining yet another copy of the grammar will be accepted by a naive reviewer and will drift again. There is no test coverage for latency_cache_path at all.
problem: auto_router/settings.py contains two readers of the same SQLite URL grammar and they do not agree. `validate_database_placement` is the canonical resolver and documents the deployment contract in its own comments: `sqlite:///data/x` means the absolute persistent mount `/data/x`, while `sqlite:///./data/x` stays workdir-relative. `Settings.latency_cache_path` predates that resolver and still re-implements the grammar: for a bare-relative path it joins against the process working directory. So with database_url=sqlite:///data/router.sqlite3 the placement guard reports `persistent: true` and the operator sees a passing check, while the per-node latency EMA cache is written to <cwd>/data/latency_ema.json -- the container writable layer, which is discarded on every container recreation, so the router re-learns node snappiness from cold forever. That is the exact drift class the placement guard exists to prevent. Repair the module so both readers resolve a configured URL the same way and the EMA file always lands beside router.sqlite3.
title: The latency EMA cache resolves database URLs differently from the placement guard
